what: A screen-covering curtain drawn with four vertices. When a same-site link is clicked, the curtain fills up from the bottom. The two front-edge vertices move separately (one leads by .54s as a curve, the other trails by .03s at .6s Quart.inOut), covering the screen with a slanted edge before navigating. On the new page, the two back vertices of the covering curtain gather upward, .63s and .07s late over .7s, lift away along a slanted edge, then fire fx:done. For left-right direction, the edge bulges as a quadratic curve (About panel open)

options.in · out: Cover length · uncover length (seconds), default .6 · .7 — 0 switches instantly
options.in-dir · out-dir: Covering side and wiping side — top (default)·bottom·left·right. Can be changed per link with data-wipe-dir
options.start: If off, does not clear on first open (the curtain is hidden from the start) — after the loader, el.fxReveal('top') when traversing directly
options.data-wipe=skip: Attach to a link to go straight through with no curtain (.prevent works the same)
options.links: If off, it does not intercept link presses (when you call the veil yourself) — if a page has two or more veils, turn on only one

note: Only one curtain element directly under body. After the lift, fx:done — the side that connects with the loader is set to start: off, and calls el.fxReveal(direction) after the loader ends. The original is a 2d canvas, here a screen-size SVG path

from.where: shared.js (TransitionCanvas — link transition, reveal after the loader, ABOUT panel left and right)
